memory_update.text: ANET is a core direct candidate for the AI Ethernet switching systems layer; prioritize verification of AI-specific networking revenue, 800G/1.6T mix, and cloud concentration.
AVGO is a core direct candidate across custom AI ASICs, Ethernet switching/routing, NICs, PCIe, and optical interconnect; its node exposure is broad but needs revenue disaggregation.
MRVL is a core direct candidate for AI optical DSPs, DCI modules, SerDes, PCIe/CXL connectivity, Ethernet switching silicon, and custom AI silicon.
COHR is a core optical candidate for AI data-center photonics, transceivers, lasers, CPO/pluggable roadmap, and optical circuit switching.

ALAB is a direct high-growth connectivity candidate for rack-scale AI systems, especially PCIe, CXL, Ethernet, UALink, NVLink Fusion-related connectivity, active cable modules, and connectivity software.

CSCO was not included due to the five-candidate limit but remains an obvious leader to test in a broader networking systems pass, especially Silicon One, Nexus, AI PODs, optics, and hyperscaler AI infrastructure orders.

LITE and FN were not included due to the five-candidate limit but remain important optical supply-chain candidates: Lumentum for lasers/transceivers and Fabrinet for optical module manufacturing/advanced packaging.

The AI networking chokepoint should be split into at least four subnodes for later scoring: Ethernet switching systems, merchant/custom networking silicon, optical DSPs/interconnect silicon, and optical modules/components/manufacturing.

node: AI data-center networking: Ethernet, optical, switching, and interconnect
summary: Expanded the US-listed universe for the AI data-center networking node to five high-directness candidates across Ethernet switching systems, custom/networking silicon, optical DSP/interconnect silicon, optical modules/components, and rack-scale connectivity. This is a research universe only, not a ranking or trading recommendation. The strongest direct exposure candidates are Arista Networks, Broadcom, Marvell Technology, Coherent, and Astera Labs. Cisco, Lumentum, Fabrinet, and other optical/component names remain coverage gaps for a later wider pass because the candidate limit is five.
